author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, named first name then last name. It presents specialties, not the veterinarian roster, and shows all of them on one page.
acceptance_criteria: The specialty page is served at GET /specialties.html and is reachable by that address alone; no other page of the system links to it and no navigation entry is added.
Every specialty the clinic knows is listed, by its stored name, with the veterinarians holding it.
A veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it as first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown against it.
All specialties render on one page; the page is not paged.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is shown under each of them.
Specialties are presented in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians within each specialty.

The page's own fixed wording is externalized and translated like every other page (REQ-LANG-002), and it carries the standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001). Specialty and veterinarian names are stored data, shown as stored.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged; this page is read-only
A navigation entry or a link from any other page — deferred to a possible follow-up request
Searching or filtering by specialty — NG-9 stands; the page is a listing, not a search
Changing the existing paged veterinarian list (REQ-VET-001) or its routes
notes: Slice scope: PRD section "Specialty directory" in docs/prd.md, requirement REQ-VET-003, edge cases 1-3. The route GET /specialties.html is the product owner's verbatim decision and is carried here rather than in the PRD, which names no routes; record it in system-design.md. Two questions were left open per the product owner's instruction to take the narrowest reading and record rather than block: (1) which ordering the stable order should be — alphabetical, stored, or other; (2) when the page gets a visible entry point. Narrowest readings taken: "every specialty" includes one no veterinarian holds; stability of order is required because the acceptance criteria must be deterministic, but the specific ordering is not specified.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely in the existing vet feature package and reuses the recorded page shape (feature package, no service layer, Thymeleaf layout fragment, repository read straight from the controller). It is new design ground on one axis only: the Vet-Specialty association is unidirectional and no SpecialtyRepository exists, so a specialty no veterinarian holds is unreachable from the veterinarian graph. Recorded as ADR 2026-08-23-specialty-side-reads-invert-in-memory: both sides are read independently and inverted in memory by a new SpecialtyDirectory value object, which also fixes the presentation order in Java so it does not vary with database collation. system-design.md gains Contracts rows for SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory, an invariant paragraph on the unidirectional association, and the route-and-reachability paragraph the prd-entry asked to be recorded.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html served by a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package, returning view name vets/specialtyList. It is a second HTTP surface, not a second route on VetController: the Web controller row of architecture-principles admits one surface per controller, the naming rule prefixes a controller with its domain noun, and the owner package already splits per noun (Owner/Pet/Visit). This supersedes the prd-entry file_targets guess of VetController and VetControllerTests.

SpecialtyRepository extends the bare org.springframework.data.repository.Repository typed to Specialty, exposing one read method annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true). VetRepository is the precedent, not PetTypeRepository: the bare interface exposes no save or delete, so NG-2 (no management of vets or specialties) holds by construction rather than by convention.

Veterinarians are read through the existing VetRepository.findAll(), which is already @Cacheable("vets") and whose Vet.specialties association is FetchType.EAGER. spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, so the graph must be complete before rendering; the eager mapping already guarantees that for this direction. Add no new cache and no new @Cacheable annotation.

The template renders through th:replace of fragments/layout :: layout, so the page carries the standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001). Pass a menu argument that matches no existing menu item (for example 'specialties'); the layout compares ${active==menu}, so no nav item renders as active. Do not pass 'vets'.
fragments/layout.html is read-only for this slice, and no existing template gains a link. The nav bar gains no specialties item (REQ-VET-003, no entry point).

patterns.description: SpecialtyDirectory is a Value object: immutable, equal by value, defensive copies of its collections, no framework instantiation, so the persistence-entity exception does not apply and the closed properties bind it in full. Domain noun, no suffix, per the naming table.

Vet.getSpecialties() already sorts by name in Java. SpecialtyDirectory uses the same approach one level up: specialties ordered by name, veterinarians within a specialty ordered by last name then first name, both in the value object's factory rather than in SQL.

Existing display idiom for a veterinarian's name: ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}. Reuse it in the new template rather than adding a name-composition method; SpecialtyDirectory holds the veterinarians, the template composes the name.

REQ-LANG-002 is satisfied by reusing existing keys where the wording fits (specialties, vets, name) so no translation debt is added. Any genuinely new key must be added to messages.properties and to all nine locale bundles except messages_en.properties, which is the fallback; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on both a literal string in a template and a key missing from a bundle.

risks.risk: The implementer maps the inverse side (@ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty) as the obvious way to answer the specialty-side question. That creates a reference cycle through Vet, which VetController's serialized /vets route marshals.
risks.mitigation: ADR 2026-08-23 records the rejection and the reason; the association stays unidirectional and the inversion happens in SpecialtyDirectory.

risks.risk: Ordering delegated to SQL (ORDER BY in a @Query, as PetTypeRepository does) would be decided by database collation, which already diverges across the three vendor schemas (system-design.md Known Defects, PostgreSQL case sensitivity). The order assertion would then be vendor-dependent and only H2 is exercised by the default suite.
risks.mitigation: Order in Java inside SpecialtyDirectory; the repository read is unordered.

risks.risk: A specialty no veterinarian holds renders as a row with nothing against it, and an implementer may reach for the existing #{none} key as the vet list does.
risks.mitigation: The acceptance criterion says the specialty is listed with no veterinarian shown against it, not with placeholder wording. Render nothing. Narrowest reading, recorded as an open question below.

risks.risk: PetClinicRuntimeHints registers Java serialization for BaseEntity, Person and Vet for the native image. A new cached or serialized type would need a hint, and the native build is not in the default test path.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory is built per request and never cached or serialized, so no hint is needed. Adding a cache for it would change that.

notes: REQ-LANG-002 / REQ-SYS-001 adjudication, as requested. The dependency is real but it does not imply an entry point, because the two obligations are directional. REQ-SYS-001 is an inbound property of the new page: every page carries navigation to the owner and veterinarian areas, which this page satisfies by rendering through fragments/layout.html like every other page. The product decision is an outbound property: nothing links to the page. The layout's nav bar gains no specialties item and no existing template gains a link, while the specialty page displays the same Home / Find owners / Veterinarians / Error bar as the rest of the system. The page carries the navigation; the navigation does not carry the page. REQ-LANG-002 binds only the page's own fixed wording, which is externalized into the bundles; it says nothing about linking. Both dependencies are therefore honored with fragments/layout.html unmodified, and neither is in tension with the product owner's decision. Recorded in system-design.md under Contracts. Open questions carried forward, not blocking, per the product owner's instruction to take the narrowest reading: (1) which stable order is wanted -- narrowest reading taken is specialties by name ascending and veterinarians by last name then first name, following the project's existing name-ordering convention in Vet.getSpecialties() and PetTypeRepository, applied in Java for vendor independence; a different order later changes SpecialtyDirectory only. (2) When the page gets a visible entry point -- deferred; adding one is a one-line menuItem in fragments/layout.html plus one message key in ten bundles. (3) Whether an unheld specialty should show placeholder wording -- narrowest reading is nothing. For the test-strategist: the existing VetControllerTests uses @MockitoBean, which contradicts the no-mocks rule in CLAUDE.md and testing-principles.md. Do not copy that idiom into the new tests; SpecialtyDirectory exists partly so the grouping, the ordering, the multi-specialty veterinarian, the unheld specialty and the unspecialized veterinarian are all assertable against real objects with no database and no MVC context, leaving the controller test to assert only the route, the view name and the rendered names. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory is a true immutable value object: private constructor, List.copyOf/Map.copyOf defensive copies, value-based equals/hashCode, matching by stored identity (getId()) as the ADR requires since BaseEntity compares by object identity
SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository interface with a single @Transactional(readOnly = true) findAll(), matching VetRepository's shape and honoring NG-2 (no write path)
SpecialtyController is package-private, constructor-injected, single-responsibility, and delegates all grouping/ordering logic to SpecialtyDirectory rather than doing it inline
Ordering comparators (BY_NAME, BY_LAST_THEN_FIRST_NAME) are documented with the collation rationale and applied in Java, not SQL

specialtyList.html composes the full name via ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}, matching the existing vetList.html idiom exactly; no new i18n keys needed since 'specialties', 'name', 'vets' already exist in messages.properties

Javadoc throughout (SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController) explains the why (unidirectional association, ADR reference, per-vendor collation) not just the what
./gradlew checkFormatMain and checkFormatTest both pass (note: the task name is checkFormatMain/checkFormatTest in this project, not checkJavaFormat)

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection surface: no SQL, JPQL, or native query is introduced. SpecialtyRepository declares a single derived findAll() on the bare Spring Data Repository interface, so no string-concatenated query text exists; consistent with the SQL-injection mitigation row in docs/system-design.md Threat Model.

Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (specialty.name, vet.firstName/lastName) with Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping. Swept all templates under src/main/resources/templates for th:utext, utext, and th:inline - zero hits, so the slice introduces no unescaped sink and no deviation from vetList.html's established pattern.

No user input: GET /specialties.html takes no path variable, query parameter, request body, or header. There is no binder, no @RequestParam, and no attacker-controlled value reaching the model, so template/expression injection and path traversal have no entry point. The menu selector 'specialties' passed to fragments/layout is a template literal, not input.

Write path: SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository interface (not CrudRepository/JpaRepository) and declares only findAll() with @Transactional(readOnly = true). No save, delete, or flush is reachable through it, and no existing entity mapping was altered, so the slice adds no state-changing surface and no CSRF-relevant route.

Data exposure: the page renders specialty names and veterinarian first/last names, all of which /vets.html and the serialized /vets route already publish. The only value not previously reachable is the name of a specialty no veterinarian holds - a clinic lookup value, not PII and not operational detail. No identifiers, credentials, or internal state are leaked; IllegalArgumentException in veterinariansHolding is unreachable by construction (every listed specialty is a map key), so no error-path stack trace exposure.

Access control: the route inherits the application-wide unauthenticated posture already recorded in docs/system-design.md Security Context and Threat Model. It is a read-only page over data already served anonymously on two existing routes, so it neither widens the documented gap nor creates a new trust boundary. Unlinked-but-reachable adds no exposure of its own here, since the data is public on the linked /vets pages.
Secrets: swept the full change set for token/password/secret/key/credential/passwd/apikey. No hits in the added Java, template, or test sources; no property, compose, or manifest file is touched.

Supply chain: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows no build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle wrapper, or lockfile in the change set, and git status reports those paths clean. No dependency is added, upgraded, or pinned, so the slice introduces no new CVE surface and no framework-version change to check against NVD.
